Result: "---\nname: unit-test-review\ndescription: 'EDK II / AMI unit test code review (MANDATORY when IS_UNIT_TEST_REVIEW = TRUE). Covers framework structure standards, test case coverage assessment, and AMI coding standards for unit test source. Invoked automatically in Stage 3 Step 3.10 when unit test files are detected in the diff.'\nuser-invocable: false\ndisable-model-invocation: false\n---\n\n# Unit Test Code Review — AMI / EDK II Framework (MANDATORY when IS_UNIT_TEST_REVIEW = TRUE)\n\n## Purpose\n\nValidate unit test source code in an MR against:\n1. **Framework structure standards** — correct use of the EDK II `UnitTestFrameworkPkg` / cmocka framework and AMI-specific structural rules\n2. **Test case coverage** — adequate scenario coverage against the production functions being tested\n3. **AMI coding standards** — AMI-specific style and hygiene rules that apply to unit test source\n\n**Standards source:** AMI unit test development rules (`copilot-instructions.md`, Rules #1–#20, Sections 3–4) and the standard EDK II `UnitTestFrameworkPkg` framework conventions.\n\n**Compliance level:**\n- Framework structure violations and coverage violations → scored into the main verdict (MAJOR violations can cause BLOCK)\n- AMI coding standards for unit tests → MINOR severity (per rule scope); do not block on style alone\n- **Severity cap: maximum MAJOR for all `HOST_APPLICATION` unit test findings** — `CRITICAL` requires confirmation that the unit test code is included in a firmware binary (verify FDF/DSC inclusion chain before assigning)\n\n---\n\n## When to Use\n\n- **Automatically** — when `IS_UNIT_TEST_REVIEW = TRUE` (set by Stage 1 Gate G9); invoked in Stage 3 Step 3.10\n- **Files in scope:** All files in the diff where the path contains `UnitTest/`, `GoogleTest/`, or the filename matches `*UnitTestHost.c`, `*UnitTestMock.c`, or `*UnitTestHost.inf`\n- **Skip:** Production source files (`.c`/`.h` under non-test paths), firmware INFs/DSCs/FDFs unrelated to unit test builds\n\n---\n\n## Validation Procedure\n\nApply the three sections below in order. Each produces findings that are appended to `Detailed_Review_Report.md` in Step 3.10. All findings are tagged `[UNIT-TEST]` to distinguish them from firmware findings.\n\n---\n\n## Section 1 — Framework Structure Standards\n\n### 1.1 — File Separation Rule (Rule #17 / File Separation Rule)\n\n**What to check:** Verify the test driver file layout is correct.\n\n| Rule | Violation | Severity |\n|------|-----------|----------|\n| `*UnitTestHost.c` must contain test cases and suite setup/teardown ONLY | Mock implementations (cmocka `__wrap_*`, stub functions, `will_return`/`expect_value` setup that belongs in the mock layer) present in `*UnitTestHost.c` | **MAJOR** |\n| `*UnitTestMock.c` must contain all mock implementations ONLY | Test cases (`UNIT_TEST_STATUS EFIAPI ...`) or suite setup/teardown functions present in `*UnitTestMock.c` | **MAJOR** |\n| One test driver per module — `*UnitTestHost.c` covers ALL `.c` files in the module's `[Sources]` | Multiple `*UnitTestHost.c` files for the same module without explicit justification (incompatible PEI vs. DXE contexts is the only valid exception; exception MUST be documented in a comment) | **MINOR-A** |\n| Additional production `.c` files added to the module must be added to the EXISTING `*UnitTestHost.inf [Sources]` — NOT a new `*UnitTestHost.c`/`.inf` pair | New `*UnitTestHost.c` or `*UnitTestHost.inf` created for a single new `.c` file in an existing module | **MINOR-A** |\n\n### 1.2 — INF Requirements\n\n**What to check:** Inspect each `*UnitTestHost.inf` and mock library INF in the diff.\n\n| Rule | Violation | Severity |\n|------|-----------|----------|\n| Test driver INF must have `MODULE_TYPE = HOST_APPLICATION` | `MODULE_TYPE` is any value other than `HOST_APPLICATION` | **MAJOR** |\n| `HOST_APPLICATION` INF must NOT have `[Depex]` section | `[Depex]` section present in a `HOST_APPLICATION` INF | **MAJOR** |\n| Mock library INF (`Mock*.inf`) must include `[BuildOptions]` with `MSFT:*_*_*_CC_FLAGS = /EHsc` | Missing `/EHsc` C++ exception flag on a mock INF that contains `.cpp` sources | **MINOR-A** |\n| Mock library INF `LIBRARY_CLASS` must equal `BASE_NAME` without the `Mock` prefix (e.g., `MockUefiLib.inf` → `LIBRARY_CLASS = UefiLib`) | `LIBRARY_CLASS` does not strip the `Mock` prefix | **MINOR-B** |\n| `BASE_NAME` of the test driver INF must contain the word `Test` (required for auto-discovery by test runner plugins) | `BASE_NAME` does not contain `Test` | **MINOR-B** |\n\n### 1.3 — Library Selection Hierarchy (3-Tier Rule)\n\n**What to check:** For every library class resolved in `*UnitTestHost.inf` and test DSC, verify the tier is correct.\n\n**Tier hierarchy (strictly enforced):**\n\n| Tier | When to use | Library prefix |\n|------|-------------|----------------|\n| **Tier 1 — PRIMARY** | Positive test paths — ALWAYS check first | `UnitTest*` (e.g., `UnitTestUefiBootServicesTableLib`, `UnitTestMemoryAllocationLib`, `UnitTestPeiServicesTablePointerLib`) |\n| **Tier 2 — GAP FILL** | ONLY when Tier 1 library does not exist, OR Tier 1 returns `EFI_NOT_AVAILABLE_YET` / `EFI_UNSUPPORTED` for the function being called | `Mock*` |\n| **Tier 3 — FAILURE INJECTION** | Negative tests only — forcing error returns | `Mock*` with `will_return(ErrorCode)` |\n\n| Violation | Severity |\n|-----------|----------|\n| `Mock*` library used in positive test context when a functional `UnitTest*` library exists for the same class (Tier 1 skipped without justification) | **MAJOR** — positive test does not exercise real code path |\n| `Mock*` used as Tier 2 gap fill without documented evidence that the `UnitTest*` library returns a stub value (`EFI_NOT_AVAILABLE_YET` or `EFI_UNSUPPORTED`) | **MINOR-A** — gap fill claim unverified |\n| `Token.h` present as a static file in the test directory | **MAJOR** — `Token.h` is a build-generated file; static `Token.h` will conflict with the SDK-generated version. Correct pattern: `#ifndef CONSTANT_NAME / #define CONSTANT_NAME value / #endif` guards in `*UnitTestHost.c` |\n\n### 1.4 — Internal Function Mock Prohibition (Rule #9)\n\n**What to check:** For every mock or stub function in `*UnitTestMock.c` and every `expect_value`/`will_return` in `*UnitTestHost.c`, verify the target function is NOT defined in the same production `.c` file listed in `[Sources]`.\n\n| Violation | Severity |\n|-----------|----------|\n| A function defined in the SAME production `.c` file (listed in `[Sources]`) is mocked or stubbed — regardless of mock mechanism (`__wrap_*`, cmocka stub, or `Mock*` library override) | **MAJOR** — mocking internal production functions makes the test functionally incorrect; real bugs in internal helpers are hidden from the test |\n\n**How to verify:** Check each mocked symbol name against the production source files listed in `[Sources]` of the test INF. If the symbol is defined in one of those files → MAJOR violation.\n\n### 1.5 — Suite Setup/Teardown Signatures (Rule #15)\n\n**What to check:** Every function registered as suite setup or suite teardown must have the correct signature.\n\n| Rule | Violation | Severity |\n|------|-----------|----------|\n| Suite setup/teardown prototype: `VOID EFIAPI FunctionName (VOID)` | Return type is `EFI_STATUS` instead of `VOID` — causes MSVC C4113 compiler error | **MAJOR** |\n| Suite setup/teardown prototype: `VOID EFIAPI FunctionName (VOID)` | Parameter list includes `IN UNIT_TEST_FRAMEWORK_HANDLE Framework` — wrong signature | **MAJOR** |\n| `InitUnitTestUefiSystemTableLibServices()` and `InitMockUefiSystemTableLibServices()` return `VOID` — must NOT be assigned | Return value assigned to an `EFI_STATUS` variable — causes MSVC C2186 compiler error | **MAJOR** |\n\n### 1.6 — Forward Declarations (Rule #16)\n\n**What to check:** In `*UnitTestHost.c`, check whether the test file calls any production functions that are defined in `.c` files listed under `[Sources]` of the test INF.\n\n| Violation | Severity |\n|-----------|----------|\n| `*UnitTestHost.c` calls a production function by name (without going through a mock or protocol pointer) where that function is defined in a `[Sources]` `.c` file, AND no forward declaration matching the production function's exact signature is present near the top of `*UnitTestHost.c` | **MINOR-A** — MSVC C4013 warning causes silent `int` return type assumption for pointer-returning functions; can corrupt `EFI_EVENT`, `EFI_HANDLE`, and protocol pointer return values |\n\n---\n\n## Section 2 — Test Case Coverage\n\n### 2.1 — Test Case Count (Section 4 / Rules #4A–#4B)\n\n**What to check:** For each production function under test, count the test cases registered in `AddTestCase()` calls in `*UnitTestHost.c`.\n\n| Rule | Violation | Severity |\n|------|-----------|----------|\n| At least ONE positive test case per function | No positive test case for a production function in scope | **MAJOR** |\n| At least ONE negative test case per function | No negative test case for a production function in scope | **MAJOR** |\n| Exactly ONE positive test case per function (all success paths consolidated) | More than one positive test case for the same function without documented justification | **MINOR-A** — consolidate per Rule 4A |\n| Exactly ONE negative test case per function (all error paths consolidated) | More than one negative test case for the same function without documented justification | **MINOR-A** — consolidate per Rule 4B |\n\n> **Note on \"missing\" test cases:** A function is \"in scope\" when it appears in the production source files listed under `[Sources]` of the test INF AND is not a static internal helper (those are covered through the main function's execution flow per Rule #9/#13). Trivial getters, pure wrappers, and unreachable functions are exempt — this must be documented in the review.\n\n### 2.2 — Coverage Thresholds (Rule #12)\n\n**What to check:** If coverage metrics are available in the MR (e.g., from a CI pipeline report, a coverage XML artifact, or inline comments), verify the thresholds.\n\n| Threshold | Violation | Severity |\n|-----------|-----------|----------|\n| Code coverage ≥ 90% of executable lines | Coverage reported or estimated below 90% of executable lines | **MAJOR** |\n| Branch coverage ≥ 80% of **reachable** branches | Coverage reported or estimated below 80% of reachable branches | **MAJOR** |\n\n> **\"Reachable\" branches** exclude branches pre-classified as `UNREACHABLE` (dead code: always-false conditions, code after unconditional return, `ASSERT(FALSE)` paths) or `INFEASIBLE` (host environment limitation: hardware register access, physical bus operations, SMBIOS structures unavailable on host). If the MR does not classify its dead code, flag uncovered branches as MINOR-A only (cannot distinguish UNREACHABLE from oversight without production code analysis).\n\n> **When no coverage data is available:** Do not guess coverage values. Instead, identify obvious missing scenarios: check that each `if`/`else`, each non-`EFI_SUCCESS` return path, and each `NULL` pointer guard in the production function has at least one corresponding test scenario. Flag clearly missing scenarios as MINOR-A.\n\n### 2.3 — Mock Expectation Correctness (Rule #10)\n\n**What to check:** For every `expect_value()`, `expect_any()`, `will_return()`, or `expect_ptr()` call in `*UnitTestHost.c` or `*UnitTestMock.c`, verify the expectation matches the mock implementation.\n\n**The rule:** Before writing any expectation, the mock `.c` source must be read to find:\n- All `check_expected(ParamName)` calls → each one requires a matching `expect_value()` or `expect_any()` in the test\n- Whether the function calls `mock()` for its return value → if YES, `will_return()` is required; if NO, `will_return()` must NOT be added\n\n| Violation | Severity |\n|-----------|----------|\n| `expect_value(MockFunc, Param, X)` added for a parameter that has NO `check_expected(Param)` in the mock source | **MAJOR** — causes \"still has values that haven't been checked\" test failure |\n| `will_return(MockFunc, X)` added when the mock source does NOT call `mock()` for its return value | **MAJOR** — causes \"still has values\" test failure |\n| Multiple `will_return(MockFunc, X)` calls for a single mock invocation without a corresponding second call in the test flow | **MAJOR** — causes \"still has values\" or unexpected return value |\n| `expect_value()`/`will_return()` copied from another test function without verifying the mock implementation | **MINOR-A** — high risk of incorrect expectations; requires explicit verification note |\n\n> **Review approach:** When this section identifies a suspected violation, read the mock `.c` source file to confirm before recording the finding. If the mock source is not in the diff and cannot be located in the workspace, record `[UNIT-TEST-MOCK-UNVERIFIED: <symbol> — mock source not found; expectation correctness unverifiable]` at MINOR-A.\n\n### 2.4 — Memory Allocation Failure Coverage (Rule #11)\n\n**What to check:** For each production function that calls `AllocatePool`, `AllocateZeroPool`, `ReallocatePool`, or `gBS->AllocatePool`, verify that the negative test case includes an allocation failure scenario.\n\n| Violation | Severity |\n|-----------|----------|\n| Production function allocates memory AND has a non-trivial error path on allocation failure, BUT the negative test case does not include a `will_return(AllocatePool, 0)` or equivalent `NULL` injection | **MINOR-A** — allocation failure path untested |\n\n---\n\n## Section 3 — AMI Coding Standards for Unit Test Source\n\n### 3.1 — Inline Scenario Comments (Rule #20)\n\n**What to check:** Every distinct scenario block within a test case function body must be prefixed with an inline comment in the required format.\n\n**Required format:**\n```c\n// FunctionName: brief description of what this scenario tests\n<test code for that scenario>\n```\n\n| Violation | Severity |\n|-----------|----------|\n| Scenario block present but no inline comment prefix | **MINOR-A** |\n| Inline comment present but does not follow `// FunctionName: description` format (e.g., uses a generic comment not tied to the function under test) | **MINOR-B** |\n\n**Forbidden inline comment patterns (Rule #19/#20):**\n\n| Forbidden pattern | Example | Severity |\n|-------------------|---------|----------|\n| Tier-rule annotations | `// Tier 1 — UnitTest*` · `// Tier 3 — failure injection` | **MINOR-B** |\n| Phase-label markers | `// Phase 2: setup` · `// Phase 3: negative path` | **MINOR-B** |\n| Rule number references | `// Per Rule #10 — mock expects parameter` | **MINOR-B** |\n| TODO / FIXME notes in committed test code | `// TODO: add more scenarios` | **MINOR-B** |\n| Commented-out code blocks | Blocks of `//`-prefixed non-comment code | **MINOR-B** |\n\n### 3.2 — No Standalone Brace Blocks (Rule #18)\n\n**What to check:** Scan each test case function body for standalone `{}` blocks that wrap sequential test scenario code without a controlling statement.\n\n| Violation | Example | Severity |\n|-----------|---------|----------|\n| Sequential scenario code wrapped in `{ ... }` without a controlling `if`/`for`/`while`/`switch` | `{ Status = Func(); UT_ASSERT_NOT_EFI_ERROR(Status); }` | **MINOR-B** |\n\n**Allowed `{}` uses:** function bodies, `if`/`else`/`for`/`while`/`switch` control bodies, struct/array initializers — do NOT flag these.\n\n### 3.3 — AMI Copyright Header (AMI standard)\n\n**What to check:** Every new `*UnitTestHost.c` and `*UnitTestMock.c` file added in the diff must contain the AMI copyright banner as the first non-blank block.\n\n| Violation | Severity |\n|-----------|----------|\n| Missing AMI copyright banner (`Copyright (c) 1985-YYYY, AMI`) on a new `*UnitTestHost.c` or `*UnitTestMock.c` | **MINOR-A** |\n\n### 3.4 — File Naming Conventions\n\n**What to check:** Verify that new unit test files follow the AMI naming pattern.\n\n| Rule | Violation | Severity |\n|------|-----------|----------|\n| Test host file: `<ModuleName>UnitTestHost.c` | Test host `.c` file does not end in `UnitTestHost.c` | **MINOR-B** |\n| Mock file: `<ModuleName>UnitTestMock.c` | Mock `.c` file does not end in `UnitTestMock.c` | **MINOR-B** |\n\n---\n\n## Section 4 — Severity Reference\n\n| Category | Specific Violation | Severity |\n|----------|--------------------|----------|\n| Framework | Mock implementations in `*UnitTestHost.c` / test cases in `*UnitTestMock.c` | MAJOR |\n| Framework | `MODULE_TYPE ≠ HOST_APPLICATION` on test driver | MAJOR |\n| Framework | `[Depex]` section present in `HOST_APPLICATION` INF | MAJOR |\n| Framework | `Mock*` used in positive test when functional `UnitTest*` exists (Tier 1 skipped) | MAJOR |\n| Framework | Static `Token.h` file created instead of `#ifndef` guards | MAJOR |\n| Framework | Internal production function mocked (Rule #9) | MAJOR |\n| Framework | Wrong suite setup/teardown signature (not `VOID EFIAPI ... (VOID)`) | MAJOR |\n| Framework | `InitUnitTestUefiSystemTableLibServices()` return assigned to `EFI_STATUS` | MAJOR |\n| Framework | Multiple test drivers per module without justification (Rule #17) | MINOR-A |\n| Framework | Missing `/EHsc` on mock INF `[BuildOptions]` | MINOR-A |\n| Framework | Missing forward declaration for production function (Rule #16) | MINOR-A |\n| Framework | Gap-fill Mock* use without UnitTest* stub verification (Tier 2 unverified) | MINOR-A |\n| Framework | `LIBRARY_CLASS` does not strip `Mock` prefix | MINOR-B |\n| Framework | `BASE_NAME` does not contain `Test` | MINOR-B |\n| Coverage | Code coverage < 90% of executable lines (Rule #12) | MAJOR |\n| Coverage | Branch coverage < 80% of reachable branches (Rule #12) | MAJOR |\n| Coverage | Positive test case missing for a function in scope | MAJOR |\n| Coverage | Negative test case missing for a function in scope | MAJOR |\n| Coverage | Wrong mock expectations (`expect_value` with no `check_expected`, `will_return` with no `mock()`) (Rule #10) | MAJOR |\n| Coverage | Multiple `will_return` for single call without multiple invocations | MAJOR |\n| Coverage | Allocation failure path not tested (Rule #11) | MINOR-A |\n| Coverage | More than 1 positive or 1 negative case per function not consolidated | MINOR-A |\n| Coverage | Expectations copied without mock source verification (Rule #10) | MINOR-A |\n| AMI Style | Missing inline scenario comment (Rule #20) | MINOR-A |\n| AMI Style | Missing AMI copyright banner on new test file | MINOR-A |\n| AMI Style | Inline comment wrong format (not `// FunctionName: description`) | MINOR-B |\n| AMI Style | Tier/phase/rule annotations in comments (Rule #19/#20) | MINOR-B |\n| AMI Style | TODO/FIXME in committed test code (Rule #19) | MINOR-B |\n| AMI Style | Standalone `{}` blocks around scenario code (Rule #18) | MINOR-B |\n| AMI Style | File naming convention violation | MINOR-B |\n\n---\n\n## Section 5 — Known Non-Violations (Do NOT Flag)\n\nThese patterns appear in unit test code and are **correct**. Do not flag any of the following:\n\n| Pattern | Why it is correct |\n|---------|------------------|\n| `MODULE_TYPE = HOST_APPLICATION` | Valid unit test driver type |\n| Missing `[Depex]` in a `HOST_APPLICATION` INF | `[Depex]` is not valid for `HOST_APPLICATION` |\n| `.cpp` source file extension | Valid for GoogleTest-based tests |\n| `extern \"C\" { #include <Uefi.h> }` in `.cpp` files | **Mandatory** — prevents C++ linkage errors for C headers |\n| `UT_ASSERT_EQUAL`, `UT_ASSERT_NOT_EFI_ERROR`, `UT_ASSERT_STATUS_EQUAL`, `UT_ASSERT_TRUE`, `UT_ASSERT_FALSE` | `UnitTestLib` assertion macros |\n| `will_return()`, `expect_value()`, `expect_any()`, `check_expected()` | cmocka mock framework calls |\n| `EXPECT_CALL()`, `WillOnce()`, `Return()`, `TEST()`, `TEST_F()` | GoogleTest / gMock framework calls |\n| `#include <Library/GoogleTestLib.h>`, `#include <Library/FunctionMockLib.h>`, `#include <cmocka.h>` | Framework dependency includes |\n| `MOCK_INTERFACE_DECLARATION`, `MOCK_INTERFACE_DEFINITION`, `MOCK_FUNCTION_DECLARATION`, `MOCK_FUNCTION_DEFINITION` | `FunctionMockLib` mock construction macros |\n| `using namespace testing;` in `.cpp` test files | GoogleTest namespace import — standard pattern |\n| `#ifndef TOKEN_CONSTANT / #define TOKEN_CONSTANT value / #endif` in `*UnitTestHost.c` | Correct Token.h constant replacement per Rule #6 |\n| No `EFIAPI` on C++ test functions | C++ linkage — `EFIAPI` calling convention is a C concept |\n| `InitUnitTestUefiSystemTableLibServices()` or `InitMockUefiSystemTableLibServices()` called as standalone statement (not assigned) | Correct usage — these return `VOID` |\n\n---\n\n## Section 6 — Output Format\n\nAppend the following section to `Detailed_Review_Report.md` and a condensed summary to `Review_Report.md` after Step 3.10 completes.\n\n### Detailed Report Section\n\n```markdown\n---\n\n## Unit Test Standards Review [UNIT-TEST]\n\nFiles reviewed against AMI EDK II Unit Test Framework standards (`.github/skills/unit-test-review/`).\nUnit test detection signal: `IS_UNIT_TEST_REVIEW = TRUE` — <N> unit test file(s) in diff.\n\n### Summary\n- Unit test files reviewed: <N>\n- Framework structure findings: <C>C / <M>M / <m>m / <i>I\n- Coverage findings: <C>C / <M>M / <m>m / <i>I\n- AMI coding standards findings: <C>C / <M>M / <m>m / <i>I\n\n### Goal 1 — Framework Structure Standards\n\n*(One entry per finding — use standard finding format with F-ID continuing from main review)*\n\n**F<N> — [UNIT-TEST] <Brief title>**\n- **File:** `path/to/UnitTestHost.c`\n- **Location:** [UnitTestHost.c:<line>](../../path/UnitTestHost.c#L<line>)\n- **Severity:** MAJOR / MINOR-A / MINOR-B\n- **Rule:** Rule #<N> / Section 1.<N>\n- **Finding:** <Description of the violation>\n- **Fix:** <Concrete action required>\n\n*(If no findings: \"> All framework structure rules satisfied.\")*\n\n### Goal 2 — Test Case Coverage\n\n*(One entry per finding)*\n\n**F<N> — [UNIT-TEST] <Brief title>**\n- **File:** `path/to/UnitTestHost.c`\n- **Location:** [UnitTestHost.c:<line>](../../path/UnitTestHost.c#L<line>)\n- **Severity:** MAJOR / MINOR-A\n- **Rule:** Rule #<N> / Section 2.<N>\n- **Finding:** <Description>\n- **Fix:** <Concrete action required>\n\n*(If no findings: \"> Test case coverage meets all requirements.\")*\n\n### Goal 3 — AMI Coding Standards (Unit Test)\n\n*(One entry per finding)*\n\n**F<N> — [UNIT-TEST] <Brief title>**\n- **File:** `path/to/UnitTestHost.c`\n- **Location:** [UnitTestHost.c:<line>](../../path/UnitTestHost.c#L<line>)\n- **Severity:** MINOR-A / MINOR-B\n- **Rule:** Rule #<N> / Section 3.<N>\n- **Finding:** <Description>\n- **Fix:** <Concrete action required>\n\n*(If no findings: \"> All AMI unit test coding standard rules satisfied.\")*\n\n### Unit Test Review Verdict\n\n> **Severity cap:** All findings are HOST_APPLICATION scope only. CRITICAL is not applicable unless unit test code is confirmed shipped inside a firmware binary.\n\n| Category | MAJOR | MINOR-A | MINOR-B |\n|----------|-------|---------|---------|\n| Framework Structure | <N> | <N> | <N> |\n| Coverage | <N> | <N> | <N> |\n| AMI Coding Standards | <N> | <N> | <N> |\n\n*(Findings are scored into the main verdict using the standard scoring table — each MAJOR = +5, each MINOR-A = +2, each MINOR-B = +1, ×2 multiplier for P1/P2 files)*\n```\n\n### Summary Report Section (`Review_Report.md`)\n\n```markdown\n## Unit Test Standards Review [UNIT-TEST]\n**Files reviewed:** <N> | **MAJOR:** <M> | **MINOR-A:** <mA> | **MINOR-B:** <mB>\n\n| F-ID | File | Rule | Severity | Finding |\n|------|------|------|----------|---------|\n| F<N> | `path/file.c` | Rule #<N> | MAJOR | One-line description |\n\n*(Omit table if no findings — write \"> All unit test standards satisfied.\")*\n\n> Unit test findings are scored into the main verdict. Severity cap: MAJOR maximum for HOST_APPLICATION code.\n```\n"
